slides.title: Brooding or *reflecting?*
slides.sub: Both mean turning it over in your head. Research says they aren't the same.

slides.title: Brooding
slides.body: Comparing where you are with where you think you should be, and staying stuck there. Researchers call it a passive comparison with an unmet standard.

slides.title: Reflecting
slides.body: Turning inward on purpose to work the problem. Looking for what you can understand, or what you could do next.

slides.title: What one study found
slides.body: Brooding went with more depression symptoms, at the time and later. Reflecting went with fewer over time. (Treynor, Gonzalez & Nolen-Hoeksema, 2003)

slides.title: Comparing, or solving?
slides.body: Next time a thought loops, ask which one you're doing. If it's comparing, ask: what's one thing I could try?
